hook_text: One drawing lets you build it. The other lets you see it. You need both, and squared paper makes both easy.
clip_script: A wooden tool box. First, draw it to make it. Look straight at the front: a rectangle 300 by 150, a hand hole near the top. Scale 1 to 2, so draw it 150 by 75, but write the real sizes, 300 and 150, in millimetres, each once, on thin lines with arrowheads. Feint lines first, dark outlines after. That is a working drawing: a maker can cut the panel from it. Now draw it to show it. Same front face, true shape. From each corner, a line going back at 45 degrees, one square across, one square up on the grid, all the same length, usually half the real depth. Join the ends. Suddenly it is a box in space. That is oblique projection. Holes stay as proper circles on the front face, so put them there. Working drawing to make it, oblique drawing to see it. Your rescue device needs both, and now you know how.
visual_style: Whiteboard split: left a flat dimensioned rectangle with hand hole, right the same face sprouting 45 degree depth lines on a grid into a box.
mood: Clear, step-by-step satisfaction as the flat shape becomes solid.
pacing: Working drawing built in four quick beats, then the oblique lines drawn one by one, then the pairing.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and draw a matchbox both ways on squared paper tonight.
